marta_support: FYI onboarding ticket #9874 from EU customer. They report a surge of 429s and elevated tail latency (250-600ms) starting ~2h after our GeoIP DB refresh. They say some requests are being served from us-west and hitting auth timeouts. I'm escalating because it's blocking their onboarding. Repro steps and logs below.

marta_support: REPRO STEPS:
```
1) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <cust-token>" "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate?model=text-lite" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
2) traceroute api.redwood-inference.com
3) observe x-region header in response and latency
```

marta_support: EXCERPT FROM CUSTOMER LOGS (timestamps aligned):
```
2026-03-17T09:02:11Z POST /v1/generate 429 region=us-west token_check=delayed 350ms
2026-03-17T09:02:12Z POST /v1/generate 200 region=eu-central token_ok 38ms
2026-03-17T09:05:02Z POST /v1/generate 429 region=us-west token_recheck 410ms
```

marta_support: They ran a traceroute and it shows DNS resolving to a CloudFront/anycast address that then lands in a US POP for ~40% of requests. They said clearing local DNS cache temporarily helped for a few minutes.

eli_eng_sre: Can you paste the resolver answers (dig +trace or curl --resolve) and the full response headers? I want to confirm the X-Region and any routing tags.

marta_support: Pasting header snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-region: us-west
cache-status: HIT from-cf
server-timing: edge;dur=12, origin;dur=320
```

sam_devex: :eyes: If they're hitting us-west, auth could be slower because token verification happens on eu-control which then calls back to west? That mismatch triggers extra round trips. Quick workaround: ask them to send X-Preferred-Region: eu-central in the request while we investigate.

rajesh_support: Customer wants a fix they can apply immediately. We can advise the header but also need to patch at infra level so other customers aren't impacted. Any chance this is an EDNS/client-subnet artifact? Some ISPs rewrite EDNS and cause wrong geo mapping.

clara_dns: I'm looking at the GeoIP DB we rolled ~2h ago. I see one change where ASN -> region mapping flipped for a /20 that some EU corporate ISPs use; TTL on that record is 300s but many resolvers and ISPs override to longer caching. Also noticed our NS had a recent zone change where glue TTL was left high (86400) by mistake. That could make stale mapping persist.

eli_eng_sre: Good catch. Could explain intermittent behavior. ISP caching + high glue TTL = sticky misroute for some clients. What's the rollback plan for the GeoIP DB?

clara_dns: We can push a targeted rollback of the ASN mapping and republish with shorter zone TTLs, but propagation will still be subject to upstream resolver caches. I'll trigger a GeoIP DB rollback and set an emergency shorter TTL on the relevant RR for 300s.

deploy-bot: Deployment started by clara_dns. Rollback job id: rb_20260317_02. ETA for publish: ~90s.

marta_support: Noted. Meanwhile customer reporting auth 401s too for a small percentage — likely due to routing to the wrong auth shard. Any suggestions to advise the customer so they can continue onboarding without changing DNS?

sam_devex: Two immediate customer-facing options: 1) Use X-Preferred-Region: eu-central header. 2) Use our regional endpoint eu.api.redwood-inference.com (bypasses geo routing). Suggest the regional endpoint as primary because it's simpler for clients and bypasses edge routing quirks.

rajesh_support: I messaged the customer with both options and a short curl example. Also recommended local DNS flush and increasing client-side retry/backoff to reduce 429 fanout.

eli_eng_sre: Action items for infra:
- Roll back GeoIP ASN mapping (clara_dns)
- Shorten zone TTLs for affected RRs (clara_dns)
- Add a temporary smart-routing rule to prefer eu pools for requests with eu-origin IP ranges for next 24h (eng-sre)
- Add metric/dashboard for x-region mismatches and auth error correlation (eng-platform)

clara_dns: Rollback + TTL update completed. Propagation looking good in our monitors, but we should still expect some client-side caches to be sticky for up to 24h. I've filed a follow-up to audit glue TTL misconfigs.

marta_support: Customer confirmed reduced 429s after we recommended the regional endpoint and after our rollback. They still see rare hits to us-west, likely ISP caches; they're ok to proceed with onboarding with the regional endpoint for now.

eli_eng_sre: We'll keep the smart-routing rule live for 24h and monitor. If we still see >0.5% route mismatch for EU-origin, escalate to oncall.

rajesh_support: Logging notes and ticket updated. Marking escalation resolved for now, keeping monitoring open. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

marta_support: Follow-up: let's add a short doc for support steps on GeoIP-induced misroutes (diagnostics, headers to check, quick customer remedies). I'll draft one and ping devex for review.

sam_devex: I'll help with the doc and include the regional endpoint snippet and recommended retry semantics.

clara_dns: I'll also add a pre-deploy checklist to ensure glue TTLs and zone TTLs are reviewed when GeoIP changes land.

marta_support: Closing thread — last update to ticket and notes attached.
